summary.name: Digital library
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of digital libraries: online databases of digital resources such as text, images, audio and video that offer organization, search and retrieval, covering their history, types, features, metadata, preservation and copyright.
use_cases: understanding how digital libraries are built and run
researching digital library history and concepts
learning about digital preservation of electronic materials
reviewing copyright issues for online library content
summary.what_it_does: The page is a general encyclopedia article describing digital libraries: online collections of digital text, images, audio, video and documents that offer search, organization and retrieval. It traces the history from early ideas such as Otlet's Mundaneum and Bush's Memex through the 1994 NSF/DARPA/NASA Digital Libraries Initiative. It describes types of digital libraries, including institutional repositories (naming DSpace, Greenstone, EPrints, Digital Commons, Islandora and Samvera), national library deposit collections, digital archives, and CAD model libraries. It also covers metadata, search approaches such as distributed searching and harvested metadata, digital preservation, and copyright.
notable: Covers history from Mundaneum and Memex to the 1994 Digital Libraries Initiative
Lists open-source institutional repository software such as DSpace, Greenstone, EPrints and Islandora
Explains metadata harvesting with OAI-PMH and distributed versus harvested search
Discusses copyright, legal deposit and digital preservation challenges
caveats: Encyclopedia overview, not a single software product; it does not describe one tool's pricing or platforms
Several sections are marked as needing more citations
